methods.label: Use an altitude and the 30° right-triangle property
methods.explanation:
The \(60^\circ\) angle suggests drawing an altitude, which creates a right triangle with a \(30^\circ\) angle. Let \(AB=80\), \(\angle BAC=60^\circ\), and \(AC=t\). Then \(BC=90-t\), with \(0<t<90\).

Drop the perpendicular \(CH\) to the line \(AB\). Because the angle at \(A\) is acute, \(H\) lies on ray \(AB\). In right triangle \(ACH\), the angle at \(C\) is \(30^\circ\), so
\[
AH=\frac t2,
\qquad CH^2=t^2-\left(\frac t2\right)^2=\frac{3t^2}{4}.
\]
Also, \(AH<45<80\), so \(H\) lies between \(A\) and \(B\). Applying the Pythagorean theorem to \(BCH\) gives
\[
(90-t)^2=\left(80-\frac t2\right)^2+\frac{3t^2}{4}
=6400-80t+t^2.
\]
Expanding the left side and canceling \(t^2\), we obtain
\[
8100-180t=6400-80t,
\qquad 100t=1700.
\]
Thus \(t=17\) and \(90-t=73\). These are positive and satisfy \(17+73>80\), so the resulting triangle is nondegenerate. Its sides are \(17,73,80\), and the shortest is \(\boxed{17}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
